source.excerpt: You will never win if you have to prove that you are the winner.
trail: Wikiquote’s Wayne Dyer page ↗ groups its book quotations by title, and this sentence is the third of three listed under the Pulling Your Own Strings (1978) heading — a sourced placement rather than a bare attribution. That is the anchor, and this record does not reach past it.

The Internet Archive’s catalogue record ↗ confirms the edition behind that citation: Pulling Your Own Strings, T. Y. Crowell Co., New York, 1978, ISBN 030810336X. Confirming the edition exists is not the same as confirming the sentence is inside it, and the scan is lending-restricted, which is where we stopped.

Wikipedia’s article on Wayne Dyer ↗ establishes the author: an American self-help writer and motivational speaker whose Your Erroneous Zones (1976) made him a bestseller. Pulling Your Own Strings was the book that followed it.

author.bio: Wayne Walter Dyer was an American self-help author and motivational speaker. He took an Ed.D. in guidance and counselling at Wayne State University, worked as a high-school guidance counsellor and ran a private therapy practice before Your Erroneous Zones (1976) made him one of the most widely read self-help writers in America. He published more than twenty books over the following four decades, Pulling Your Own Strings among the earliest.

context.heading: Why it mattered
lead: Pulling Your Own Strings followed Your Erroneous Zones ↗, the 1976 book that turned Dyer into one of the most widely read self-help authors in America. The sentence makes a narrow claim, and a sharper one than it first looks: that needing to be seen winning is itself the losing position, because the proving is what hands the other person control. That is the book’s subject — not being manipulated — compressed into a line.

It also shows why self-help quotations are so hard to source. They are written to be lifted, they travel without their paragraph, and the books they come from are recent enough to be in copyright and old enough to sit off the open web. That gap is what this page is honest about rather than papering over.
